The Restatement's analysis of the issues raised by A's assignment to 
c begins in § 317. Subsection (2) of that section states: "A contractual 
right can be assigned unless .... " Thus, the subsection tells us that such 
assignments are generally allowed-but with exceptions. As if often the 
case with legal rules, it is important to examine not only the primary 
statement of law but also the exceptions, of which three are stated in 
§ 317(2). 
Restatement§ (2)(b) provides an important exception-a contractual 
right cannot be assigned if "the assignment is forbidden by statute or is 
otherwise inopemtive on grounds of public policy." Many states have 
statut ,s that forbid the assignment of certain contractual rights. A 
common example is provided by statutes that restrict the ability of an 
employl e to assign her contractual rights to be paid wages by her 
employ . As for assignments 
made inoperative on grounds of public 
policy. see the materials on public policy in Chapter 6, Section 5.
